title: Electro-Mechanical/Information and Communication Technology Maintainer (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DIR IC4
raw_text:
6. MOS 2847, Electro-Mechanical/Information and Communication Technology
Maintainer (Sgt to Pvt) PMOS, DIR IC4

    a. Summary. Electro-Mechanical/Information and Communication Technology
Maintainers (EMICTM) are trained to install, diagnose, modify, and perform
field level repairs on Marine Corps information and communication technology
systems and transmissions mediums. This includes end user devices (EUD),
live and recorded broadcasting technologies, telephony, wired and wireless
network devices, optical transmissions systems and intelligence,
surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) processing systems. Electro-
Mechanical/Information and Communication Technology Maintainers are trained
to diagnose, modify, and perform field level repairs on electro-mechanical


                                           3-255                        Enclosure (1)
 3124                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



devices to include, but not limited to unmanned, robotic, and multi-function
systems involving motors, servos, actuators and like devices and their
control systems. Typical duties include the repair and modification of
ground common electro-mechanical systems and sub-systems as well as repair
and modification of information and communication technology systems and
associated peripheral and interconnection devices utilizing visible or
infrared carriers. These Marines, submit field service requests, conduct
technical research and order repair parts to restore electro-mechanical/
information and communication technology systems at an organizational or
intermediate maintenance activity. Journeyman level Maintainers, with a
minimum of three years’ experience, reconcile repair parts and records of
systems within the active and maintenance closeout phases, make
recommendations pertaining to maintenance resource allocations and guide in
the installation of digital wideband systems. Additionally, these Marines
provide quality control inspections of maintenance tasks. These Marines
guide novice Marines through non-routine maintenance tasks and develop
competencies of those Marines. Marines in this MOS may be assigned to a BIC
(within their occupational field) that has been coded with one or more DoD
Cyber Workforce Framework (DCWF) work role codes. Please reference DoDI
8140.10, DoDM 8140.10, and the MOS roadmap for additional training and
certification requirements associated with these work role codes.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

            (2) Must have normal color vision.

            (3) Must possess an EL score of 110 or higher.

            (4) Security requirement:     secret security clearance eligibility.

        (5) Must have completed one year of high school Algebra 1, Integrated
Mathematics, Mathematical Studies SL, or an equivalent course at the minimum.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the Basic Electronics Course (M092721) and the Electro-
Mechanical/Information and Communication Technology Maintenance Course
(M09DSE1), at MCCES 29 Palms, CA.

        (2) Marines must have 36 months obligated service remaining upon
graduation from the Telephone System/Personal Computer Repair Course. This
obligated service must be obtained prior to execution of PCS (DUINS) or PCA
(DUINS) orders to the course.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (q), 2800 Ground Electronics Maintenance Training and Readiness
Manual.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) 49-2011 Computer, Automated Teller, and Office Machine Repairers.

            (2) 49-9069 Precision Instrument and Equipment Repairers.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     None.

common_text: The Ground Electronics Maintenance Occupational Field includes the installation, inspection and classification, servicing, adjustment, tuning, repair, modification, recovery and evacuation, overhauling and rebuilding, and testing and calibration of electronic equipment and systems used by Marine Corps ground forces. The equipment includes various types of communications transmission systems, information technology systems, intelligence processing systems, tactical sensor systems, cryptographic devices, artillery electronics systems, digital fire control systems, unmanned vessel electronics, miscellaneous non-communication systems, robotic and various electro-mechanical systems, electronic jamming systems, and a wide range of test equipment and calibration required devices. Qualifications to work in this field include manual dexterity, normal color vision, be eligible to hold a secret security clearance, the ability to understand highly technical material, and to comprehend complex mathematical and logic principles. Types of entry-level jobs available include work as a Ground Electronics Transmission Systems Maintainer, Ground Electronics Telecommunications and Information Technology Systems Maintainer, Calibration Technician, Artillery Electronics Technician, and Digital Wideband Systems Maintainer. Formal schooling is provided to all Marines entering this field. In general, entry-level training consists of basic electronics, electronic systems fundamentals, and an equipment-oriented phase at either a Marine Corps school or other service school. Career progression training will involve related supervisory/technical level training within the field. Skill progression, skill enhancement and skill sustainment training is provided via on the job training and through both distributed learning and formal schooling. Billets for ground electronics maintenance are found throughout the Marine Corps but are concentrated within units having specific electronic or service support missions. Marines in this field may serve within GCE, ACE, MLG, MIG units and supporting establishments. Instructor billets are found at the formal schools responsible for ground electronics training. Marines entering this field will be assigned MOS 2800, Basic Ground Electronics Maintenance Marine.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
